rubric_notes: Complete: release, lineage, all families with sunids, full a.22.1.3 membership, homology/annotation endpoints cited; deepest shared level identified as superfamily a.22.1 supporting probable common ancestry but not shared biochemical function; only core histones and macro-H2A.1 share the family; H1/H5 handled as different fold with no positive claim and explicit refusal to call analogous; enzymes and fragment excluded; heterodimer pairing labelled as general knowledge; limits on search truncation and periodic release stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Full verified lineage for both domains, homology and annotation records cited correctly. Concludes superfamily-level probable common ancestry, explicitly declines a family-level claim, notes no alignment evidence retrieved, and refuses to transfer HisE substrate/reaction/pathway or to read the unidentified 'li, unl' ligand as a substrate. States the external evidence required. All criteria met.

Families, sunids, fold, superfamily, homology record and duplication comment all correct and supported. Reasoning is complete: superfamily-level common ancestry, no family-level claim, rejects substrate/reaction/role/regulation/ligand transfer and template use, explicitly avoids analogy framing. Minor evidentiary gap: representative SIDs d1rgia1, d4foea1, d1r59o1 are said to be 'taken from search results' but no search response is in the bundle (the SIDs themselves are consistent with 2.08). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Strong hierarchy and homology reading: superfamily-level common ancestry, divergent chemistry across three families, explicit rejection of both same-activity and convergence readings, correct handling of ligand comments on d1r03a_ and d1jkua_ as crystallographic not functional, R1 and heme catalase name hits flagged. Falls short on stating what family-specific experimental evidence is required for metal/reaction claims (only notes missing BLAST/FATCAT). The periodic update label '2.08-2026-08-16 (shown in service info)' is not supported by any endpoint in the bundle.

Correct hierarchy and sunids, superfamily homology scope read as probable common ancestry only, ephrin family comment and superfamily copper comment used, copper and electron transfer not inferred. Queried the PAD4 protein node (110108, no comments) rather than the family node, so missed the 'lacking the metal-binding site' annotation, and does not state what evidence (conserved ligand geometry, biochemical data) would be needed to establish metal or redox function. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly places d.15.1.1, d.15.1.2, d.15.1.5 under superfamily d.15.1 in fold d.15 with sunids verified by the bundle; interprets superfamily as probable common ancestry and a shared beta-grasp core, not shared function; explicitly rejects transfer of conjugation chemistry, UBX binding partners and Ras-GTP binding across families; notes member heterogeneity (supported by children calls); names required external evidence and search limits. No material error. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Names all three families, superfamily c.23.1, fold c.23, with sunids verified via children/parents endpoints. States superfamily-level probable common ancestry, no family-level claim, fold/class alone insufficient. Uses the retrieved 'lacks canonical receiver domains features' comment to reject KaiA phospho-signaling, rejects clock-role transfer, ODC-wing catalysis (c.67.1.5/d.125.1 elsewhere), shared substrate/phospho-site, and template interchange. Notes Pfam mapping is automated. Release pinned to 2.08 stable.

Full lineage b > b.84 > b.84.5 > b.84.5.1 with sunids, all five b.84 superfamilies, homology records (sf scope, no warnings) and the fold-level 'homology not implied above superfamily' warning, all supported by the bundle. Correctly frames separate superfamily as absence of a positive homology assertion rather than evidence of non-relation; family groups V1/A1 bulge entries; function not inferred; limits stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct f.21 split with sunids; cites the fold homology warning, the f.21.1, f.21.2, f.21.3 and f.21.2.2 annotations (including 'may or may not contain heme'), and FdnI gamma in f.21.1.1, all bundle-supported. Explicitly frames the split as absence of a positive assertion, forbids calling them analogous/convergent/unrelated, treats the possible-link note as non-merging, and requires outside alignment/structural evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy, sunids, homology scopes, and annotations supported by bundle. Interprets superfamily as probable common ancestry, denies family-level closeness, refuses cofactor/channel-role transfer, treats family names as labels, and avoids non-homology claims. Noncentral imprecision: it says the ADH C-terminal domain 'should not be read as an independent domain', a misreading of the curator comment (it is a separate SCOP domain); protein-node labels cited are not in this bundle though accurate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family placement and identifiers, with function-transfer and ligand caveats. Cites a comparison result ('same_family', 'caveats_present false') that is not in the evidence bundle; the 'caveats_present false' claim is unsupported and sits awkwardly against the family node's 'not a true family' annotation, which the answer never retrieved. Also says the API does not state whether the family reflects natural ancestry, when the family annotation addresses this. Bio capped at 2; factual 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 own fold/superfamily vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 under c.23.14 (also confirmed in 2.08-2026-08-16), 1f8y unchanged. States shared superfamily is SCOPe's assertion of probable common ancestry, family not shared, hierarchy placement not a claim of shared catalysis, ligand not transferable. Notes SID change with same sunid and uninspected l.1.1.1 domain. Fully bundle-supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Identifies d1a14h2 as H:1-8, sunid 343393, sccs l.1.1.1 in class l Artifacts > Tags > N-terminal Tags > Synthetic; cites artifact_not_homology_evidence warning and homology_implied_by_level=false, all supported by bundle. Names d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 as the biological domain. Correctly rejects tag similarity as homology evidence and states limits (ligand comment not function, artifact placement not evidence of non-homology elsewhere). All must_include met, no must_avoid violations.

Correct 1.75 one domain f.11.1.1 and 2.08 split to b.179.1.1 and f.60.1.1 with boundaries and full lineages from bundle. Appropriately refuses to assert independent origins or that the 1.75 call was wrong, and gives sound per-segment search guidance. Compares only 1.75 and 2.08, omitting the 2.04 split release.

Correct five-domain table with SIDs/boundaries; four reused superfamilies vs Prp8-specific fold d.394 for a5 (A:47-697); uses fold annotation comment and homology warning from bundle; notes a4 bromodomain family placement as closest link without function transfer; appropriate caveats on 'newly observed' and absence of alignment evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Full interpretation: family placement on the ~34-residue repeat unit, length tracking repeat number, and the 're' flag recording intended variation. Lengths are supported by its sequence bundle, but the annotation and homology details (single-repeat comment, 're' flags, homology_scope px) are asserted without the corresponding annotation/homology endpoints in its bundle, though the values are correct.

Correct metadata supported by bundle; cites stable 2.08 pinned via /releases/2.08 and says to record the full periodic label if used; periodic does not replace stable. Describes the periodic label imprecisely as a 'refresh of the current release metadata' and omits that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting older domains. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Strong evidence use: a.47.2.1 lineage for all chains, fragment comment and 'ms' flag, automated-match provenance of d1dn1b_, obsolescence by 3c98, curated d3c98b_ with no caveats, and sequence lengths 120/124/222 with the N-terminal overlap correctly described (bundle sequences confirm S/C difference near residue 119). Reasoning correctly limits fragment-based calls to the three-helical region and uses 1dn1 B to show the fragments are part of a longer domain; notes spectrin comment is a similarity note, not homology. Stops short of stating that the complete domain resolves the earlier fragment-driven resemblance and supports the STAT-like fold interpretation. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correctly distinguishes superfamily-level divergence within c.2.1 (12 families plus automated matches, all verified) from the absence of any homology assertion between folds c.2 and c.3, and refuses to call them convergent without outside evidence. Explains convergence from physical constraint, cofactor switching within homologs, and the need for whole-domain sequence, superposition with topology, and phylogenetic support. Homology record (scope sf, no warnings) verified. Limits clearly stated. No material issue.

Clear release-change framing: 2.04 fold difference (class only shared) to 2.08 shared superfamily b.18.1 with distinct families, superfamily common-ancestry claim SCOPe did not make in 2.04, no function transfer, premise correction. Honest on weak FATCAT linkage and no residue mapping.

Retains family-level homology, correctly reads hf as domain-scoped non-inherited fold difference with similar sequence/SSE count, and usefully flags the tension between shared a.4 lineage and the hf note. Rejects template transfer and function transfer, requires residue mapping, and recommends same-group splits with a labelled hf stratum or exclusion for fold-level labels. States limits (no alignments, quality, history). All identifiers, lineage, comments and homology fields supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. All must_include met: shared b.1.2.1 homology retained (homology_implied_by_level true, no warnings); fr flag correctly described as domain-scope, not inherited, 'missing more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence'; alignment treated as partial coverage with gaps not scored as divergence and no use as full-length template; d1uc6a1 chosen as default representative on annotation grounds with d1o5dt2 retained as a labelled incomplete diversity member. Correctly notes the near-equal residue ranges (104 vs 99) do not explain the flag. Explicitly declines quality ranking since SPACI not retrieved, rejects cr9 ligand/function transfer, and lists next evidence steps. Release 2.08, sunids, boundaries, protein nodes all match the evidence bundle. No material errors.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. New superfamily (with its obligatory family) in the existing fold; family under an existing superfamily correctly rejected; new fold rejected as a wrong structural claim; negative part of superfamily placement treated as a default, not proof of nonhomology; checks for remote homology and competing superfamilies; no function transfer. Claims to have retrieved the service index with 2.08-stable and 2.08-2026-08-16, but the evidence bundle is empty.

All classification facts (d.144.1/56112 in fold d.144, class d; families 56171, 64411 with members 103302 and 64412, 88854; homology responses with no warnings; p85 subunit domains in d.93.1.1, h.4.21.1, b.34.2.1) are supported by the bundle. Interprets shared superfamily as probable common ancestry of the catalytic core, distinct families as no closer claim, and explicitly says SCOPe does not establish substrate, reaction specificity or regulation; labels the phosphotransfer mechanism as background knowledge. Rejects nonhomology as well. Requires complex structures, residue-level alignment of recognition and catalytic residues, kinetics/substrate panels, mutagenesis, regulatory-domain and partner evidence, and notes superfamily placement says nothing about domain boundaries or other domains in the chain. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
